Shows Waze and Amap turn-by-turn prompts on the car\'s instrument cluster / HUD: only while connected to a car, it reads the distance, turn and arrival text on those two apps\' navigation screens. No other app is read, and nothing is logged or uploaded.
Show turns on supported instrument clusters. Amap and Waze need accessibility access.

DroidCar is an unofficial, experimental project: it lets a non-rooted Android phone act as a CarPlay sender (the iPhone role), showing a car launcher and third-party apps from the phone on a supported receiver, and feeding the receiver\'s touch input back into virtual displays on the phone.\n\nThis project is not affiliated with Apple Inc. or any car manufacturer, has no authorization or certification of any kind, and is not an MFi-certified product. \"CarPlay\" and \"AirPlay\" are trademarks of Apple Inc., used here only to describe compatibility; this implies no affiliation or endorsement.
Work in progress — things may break at any time

This is a development build. Features, UI and the protocol implementation may change at any time, and there may be undiscovered bugs. No stability, compatibility or availability is promised.

The only combinations that have been tested are:
· Sender: Honor Magic7 Pro (Android 17)
· Receiver: Audi MIB3 head unit (real car)
· Receiver: DiPlay test bench on a Redmi K40 (Android 13)

Other phones, Android versions and car models have not been verified. They may not work at all, or may show display glitches, misaligned touches or repeated disconnects.

"Force landscape" requires Android 14 or later; it is not available on Android 13 and earlier (the settings panel says so).
